name: Illinois
agency: Illinois Secretary of State, Driver Services Department
permitAge: 15 (written test and instruction permit; secondary sources). Under 18 needs parental consent and school enrollment.

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night, with a parent or licensed adult 21 or older (GHSA, secondary)
teen.holdPermit: 9 months without a moving violation; a violation or suspension stops the clock (secondary)
teen.nightLimit: Under 18: Sunday to Thursday 10 p.m. to 6 a.m., Friday and Saturday 11 p.m. to 6 a.m., with exceptions such as driving with a parent or to work (Illinois Legal Aid Online)
teen.passengerLimit: First 12 months of license, under 18: no more than one passenger under 20, siblings and the driver's children not counted (Illinois Legal Aid Online, GHSA)
teen.phone: Under 19 with a permit or graduated license: no phone at all, hands-free included, except an emergency call. All drivers: hand-held phone banned since January 1, 2014.

bac.under21: any detectable amount (zero tolerance, 625 ILCS 5/11-501.8); first violation 3-month suspension, refusal 6 months

notes: Handbook URL is the 2024 Rules of the Road PDF on ilsos.gov, found through a search result; not confirmed as current, and no 2025 PDF was found.
A Spanish edition of Rules of the Road 2024 exists (library catalog record), but no official URL was found. Whether the knowledge test is offered in Spanish was not found.
Test format 35 questions, 28 correct (80 percent) comes from commercial practice-test sites, not from ilsos.gov.
Scott's Law (625 ILCS 5/11-907(c)): slow down, change lanes if possible; since Jan. 1, 2017 covers any stopped vehicle with flashing hazard or warning lights (Illinois State Police).
School bus: stop at least 20 feet before it; on a road with at least two lanes in each direction only same-direction traffic must stop (Illinois State Police, Aug. 2025).

Speed (625 ILCS 5/11-601): urban district 30 mph, alley 15 mph, 55 mph on other roads outside urban districts, 65 mph on designated four-lane divided highways, up to 70 mph on rural interstates since 2014.
Hand-held phone fines 5 first offense up to 50 fourth (2013-2014 news sources; may have changed).
Secondary only, not used in questions: driver education required if under 17 years 3 months; course of 30 classroom hours and 6 behind-the-wheel hours; permit fee 0; three test attempts per year.
Official ilsos.gov pages could not be read (fetch blocked); every fact here comes from search snippets.
